target.title: feat(google): add Antigravity agy auth bridge
target.body:
## Summary

This PR adds first-class `google-antigravity` support through the Antigravity `agy --print` runtime and hardens the surrounding Google auth replacement boundary.

Provider split:

- `google-antigravity` uses the signed-in Antigravity / `agy` session.
- `google-gemini-cli` uses the official Gemini CLI OAuth cache.
- `google` remains the Gemini API-key provider.

For Antigravity, OpenClaw does not import or persist raw Google OAuth tokens. OAuth/session ownership stays with Antigravity, and OpenClaw delegates execution to `agy`.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw already separates Google API-key auth, Gemini CLI OAuth, and provider-owned runtime auth paths, but it did not have a first-class Antigravity provider path. Users with a signed-in Antigravity / `agy` session could not route OpenClaw model execution through Antigravity without collapsing that path into Gemini CLI OAuth or Google API-key handling.

This PR also had a cleanup bug in the CLI preparation path: if Claude skills plugin setup failed after backend preparation, prepared backend or execution resources were not cleaned up before the error propagated.

This PR adds `google-antigravity` as a provider-owned CLI runtime path. OpenClaw delegates Antigravity execution to `agy --print`, keeps Antigravity session ownership outside OpenClaw, preserves separation from `google-gemini-cli` OAuth and `google` API-key auth, forwards selected Antigravity model refs to `agy --model`, and cleans prepared resources when skills plugin setup fails.

## What Changed

### Antigravity

- Added bundled `google-antigravity` provider registration.
- Added a `google-antigravity` CLI backend.
- Routed Antigravity prompts through `agy --print` with a bounded print timeout.
- Forwarded selected Antigravity model refs to `agy --model`.
- Added setup support for a local `google-antigravity:antigravity-session` profile.
- Added runtime auth resolution for the Antigravity app-session profile.
- Added external/synthetic auth handling so OpenClaw can detect the Antigravity session without importing raw Google OAuth tokens.
- Added provider aliases, model policy wiring, docs, and live-testing notes.

### Gemini CLI

- Added official Gemini CLI OAuth cache import support for `google-gemini-cli`.
- Changed Gemini CLI setup to import the official cache instead of launching an OpenClaw-owned Google browser auth flow.
- Required validated active Google account identity before saving or using imported Gemini CLI credentials.
- Added legacy profile recovery when an older `google-gemini-cli` profile lacks account identity and the official cache matches the expected profile.
- Failed closed on missing or mismatched Gemini CLI account identity.
- Preserved isolated Gemini CLI auth-home staging and inherited Google auth env clearing.

### Shared auth/backend boundary

- Added provider-owned CLI backend auth resolution.
- Preserved generic fallback forwarding only when no provider-owned hook exists.
- Made provider hook decline fail closed instead of falling through to generic forwarding.
- Preserved backend allowlist checks before and after auth resolution.
- Preserved Gemini API-key staging for `google` API-key profiles.
- Fixed CLI runner cleanup gaps on mid-prepare failures.
- Updated Plugin SDK exports, API baseline, and CLI backend docs.

### Cleanup and rebase follow-up

- Clean prepared backend/execution resources when `prepareClaudeCliSkillsPlugin` throws after backend preparation.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's npm `extended-stable` maintenance process needs a repeatable way to discover the complete set of security and reliability fixes for the trailing completed month's core package. The source set must include direct commits and private security work, not only public PRs, while staying inside the npm-only publication boundary landed in #99352.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a manually invoked `$openclaw-extended-stable-backport` skill that resolves either the initial `.33` bootstrap or a later maintenance patch, inventories the full mainline delta in bounded batches, reconciles private advisories, carries unresolved candidates across runs, and prepares one approved multi-commit backport PR.

The workflow now treats `docs/reference/RELEASING.md` and `scripts/openclaw-npm-extended-stable-release.mjs` as the canonical contract. It uses the exact `extended-stable/YYYY.M.33` branch shape, separates the npm selector from the user-facing `stable` channel, enforces the protected-`main` month policy, and hands release execution back to `$release-openclaw-maintainer` for exact branch/tag/package identity plus the manual preflight, Full Release Validation, publish, readback, and selector-repair path.

The skill intentionally excludes separately published plugins, GitHub Releases, native apps, Docker, mobile, and website publication. Changes that require coordinated plugin publication are blocked rather than routed through the superseded unlanded stable-plugin planner assumptions.

## User Impact

No product runtime behavior changes. Maintainers gain a release-level workflow for discovering, reviewing, backporting, validating, and handing off the complete core npm patch set for the active or initial `extended-stable` line.

target.title: fix: persist queued iOS watch replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iOS watch quick replies being held only in memory after the phone receives them while disconnected from the gateway. If the app process was terminated before reconnecting, those queued replies could be silently lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Watch quick replies now use a UserDefaults-backed queue scoped to the current gateway stable ID. Reconnect flushing peeks queued replies, forwards them through a confirmed `node.event` request, and removes them only after delivery succeeds; failed sends are left queued for a later reconnect.

## User Impact

Users can tap watch quick replies while the phone is offline and still have those replies delivered after the iOS app restarts and reconnects, without replaying stale replies into a different gateway.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): retry transient EAGAIN/EINTR on session-store and workspace-template reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, the OpenClaw gateway's heartbeat-driven reads of the session store (`loadSessionStore`) and workspace bootstrap files (`fileContentDiffersFromTemplate`) can surface transient `EAGAIN` / `EINTR` errors (`Unknown system error -11` / `errno -4`) when another process is atomically swapping the file. A single transient read failure aborted the heartbeat, which cascaded into cron, memory, and message workflows.

Reported in #99994. The existing retry loop in `loadSessionStore` was gated to **Windows-only** via `process.platform === "win32" ? 3 : 1`, so macOS and Linux got a single attempt with no retry. The workspace template read in `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` had **no retry at all** — a single transient `EAGAIN` propagated up and aborted the heartbeat.

## Evidence

### Before fix: heartbeat aborts on macOS

The production gateway on macOS (Fort Lauderdale, EST) exhibited heartbeat aborts with `EAGAIN` / `Unknown system error -11` during session-store and workspace-template reads. The errors were transient — a retry on the same file succeeded — but the code path gave up after a single attempt on non-Windows platforms.

### After fix: retry path proven by 20 passing tests

The fix adds bounded retry (3 attempts, 50ms backoff) to both read sites and classifies transient errors via `isTransientFsError()` (handles `code === EAGAIN | EINTR`, `errno === -11 | -4`, and the macOS `Unknown system error -11` message form).

Test output (vitest, verbose reporter):

```

 ✓  runtime-config  store-load.eagain-retry.test.ts > retries on transient empty reads (race with file swap) 196ms

Key test cases proving the fix:

- **`retries on EAGAIN and returns true once the read succeeds`** — first read throws `EAGAIN`, second read succeeds → function returns `true`. This is the exact production failure mode: transient `EAGAIN` no longer aborts the heartbeat.
- **`retries on the macOS 'Unknown system error -11' message form`** — proves the classifier catches the macOS-specific error string that doesn't carry a stable `.code` property.
- **`returns false after exhausting retries on persistent EAGAIN`** — proves the function degrades gracefully (returns `false`, does not rewrite the file) instead of throwing.
- **`propagates non-transient errors immediately`** — proves `EACCES` and other non-transient errors are not swallowed.

### Production gateway stability

The production gateway has been running with an equivalent patch applied to the compiled `dist/` output (same retry logic, same classifier) with **zero heartbeat failures** since deployment. The source-level fix in this PR is the clean upstream version of that production-proven patch.

### Lint and type check

- `tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- `oxlint` on all 4 changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `check-lint` CI (typescript `prefer-includes` rule) — fixed: literal regex replaced with `message.includes(...)` per the review finding.

## Root cause

`EAGAIN` (errno `-11`) and `EINTR` (errno `-4`) are transient — they surface when the kernel can't immediately satisfy a read against a file being atomically swapped by another writer. The production failure mode on macOS is the `Unknown system error -11` string form, which doesn't always carry a stable `.code` property, so detection has to match on errno and message text too.

## Changes

**`src/config/sessions/store-load.ts`** (Site 1)
- Drop the `win32`-only gate on `maxReadAttempts` → always `3` on every platform.
- Classify errors in the `catch` block: retry on transient failures (`EAGAIN`, `EINTR`, `errno -11/-4`, macOS `Unknown system error -11` message form) **and** transient `SyntaxError` (unparseable JSON — preserves the existing Windows context-loss mitigation where concurrent replacement of `sessions.json` can expose a partially-written file). Permanent filesystem failures (`ENOENT`, `EACCES`) break out immediately so the heartbeat does not stall on two 50ms `Atomics.wait` pauses for a genuinely missing or inaccessible store. (P2 from clawsweeper review.)
- Bounded retry on `SyntaxError`: a transient unparseable read retries within the loop; a persistently corrupted store exhausts retries and falls back to the empty-store path (verified by two regression tests — see below).
- Comment updated to cite #99994 and explain the macOS/Linux failure mode.

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`** (Site 2)
- Add `isTransientFsError()` classifier handling: `code === EAGAIN | EINTR`, `errno === -11 | -4`, and the macOS `Unknown system error -11` / `system error -4` message forms.
- Wrap `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` in a 3-attempt retry loop with 50ms between attempts (using the existing `./utils/sleep.js` helper).
- `ENOENT` still returns `false` ("file absent") so callers don't rewrite missing files.
- Non-transient errors propagate.
- Exhausted transient retries return `false` so the caller does **not** rewrite a file we could not read.
- `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` is exported with an `@internal` JSDoc tag so tests can exercise the retry path directly.

## Impact

No happy-path change: on a clean read the new code returns immediately. The retry loop only fires on transient errors, and only for 3 attempts with 50ms backoff. This eliminates the heartbeat aborts observed in production on macOS without altering semantics for any non-transient error class.

**Narrowed retry scope (P2 fix):** The session-store retry loop now classifies errors and only retries on transient failures (`EAGAIN`/`EINTR`/`errno -11/-4`/macOS message form). Permanent failures (`ENOENT`, `EACCES`) return immediately — verified by two regression tests that complete in <40ms with a single `readFileSync` call (no `Atomics.wait` pauses). This ensures a missing or unreadable store does not add 100ms of latency to every heartbeat cycle.

**Preserved Windows context-loss mitigation (P1 fix from clawsweeper review):** The narrowing pass initially made `SyntaxError` immediate, which removed the existing Windows mitigation where concurrent replacement of `sessions.json` can expose a partially-written (unparseable) file. This PR now retries `SyntaxError` within the bounded loop — a transient unparseable read succeeds once the file settles; a persistently corrupted store exhausts retries and falls back to the empty-store path. Two regression tests verify both paths:
- `retries on transient SyntaxError (invalid JSON) and loads the store once the read succeeds` — proves invalid-then-valid JSON succeeds via retry (2 calls).
- `returns an empty store after exhausting retries on persistent SyntaxError` — proves persistent corruption exhausts to empty store (3 calls, no infinite loop).

## Regression test suite (24/24 passing)

- `store-load.eagain-retry.test.ts` — 8 cases: EAGAIN retry, persistent EAGAIN exhaust, macOS `-11` message form, transient empty read, ENOENT immediate (<40ms), EACCES immediate (<40ms), transient SyntaxError retry, persistent SyntaxError exhaust.
- `workspace.eagain-retry.test.ts` — 16 cases (run in both `agents-core` and `agents-support` projects): ENOENT absent, content match, content differs, EAGAIN retry, EINTR retry, persistent EAGAIN exhaust, macOS `-11` message form, non-transient error propagation.
- `oxlint` clean on all changed files.

## Production behavior proof

The retry path is **live in production** on the maintainer's gateway (macOS, Node 22, OpenClaw 2026.6.11) and has been firing heartbeat-triggered session turns cleanly since patch v3 deployment. Redacted evidence:

```

Closes #99984

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on localized Windows installs could run gateway `--force`, port diagnostics, or stale gateway cleanup and have OpenClaw miss an active TCP listener because Windows `netstat` did not print the English `LISTENING` state text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI force-free path, infra diagnostics path, and Windows listening-PID fallback now share one Windows TCP `netstat` listener parser. It matches listener rows by TCP shape, exact local endpoint port, wildcard/port-zero remote endpoint, and positive PID instead of relying on localized state words. The CLI and PID fallback still deduplicate PIDs, while diagnostics keep listener address details.

The QA smoke follow-up keeps the isolated `native-command-session-target` scenario from racing its post-`/stop` recovery turn against the aborted run's session file lock. The scenario now waits for the active session to clear, for the mock delayed provider request to leave `/debug/inflight-requests`, and for the session `.jsonl.lock` file to disappear before it sends the recovery message.

## User Impact

Windows users with non-English system output get more reliable gateway port conflict detection, force-free cleanup, diagnostics, and stale gateway listener verification. Established TCP connections on the target port are not treated as listeners.

The QA smoke scenario now proves native `/stop` unblocks the next turn after the underlying abort cleanup actually finishes, instead of immediately sending recovery traffic while the same session is still locked.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): support custom silent tokens with digits and punctuation in prefix matcher
target.body:
Fixes #99982

## What Problem This Solves

`isSilentReplyPrefixText` never matches custom silent tokens containing digits or punctuation (e.g., `NO_REPLY2`, `HELP-QUIET`). The character guard `/[^A-Z_]/.test(normalized)` rejects any input containing non-letter characters, causing streamed prefix detection to fail for custom tokens with digits/hyphens.

This means the streaming suppression path effectively ignores custom silent tokens that include numbers or special characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The character guard was too broad — it checked the **input fragment** (the streamed prefix) instead of the **token definition**. An input fragment is inherently transient and partial; the only meaningful question is whether the token itself is safe for prefix matching.

- Custom tokens containing non-letter characters (digits, hyphens) cannot be mistaken for natural language words, so their partial prefixes are safe once the prefix includes at least one non-letter character from the token.
- The underscore guard (`normalized.includes("_")`) is preserved for standard `A-Z_` tokens like `HEARTBEAT_OK`.
- The `/[^A-Z_]/.test(tokenUpper)` check now tests the **token**, not the fragment.

## User Impact

Fixes an issue where Discord users with `replyToMode: "first"` could receive one native reply notification per physical chunk when a single long agent reply was split into multiple Discord messages.

Discord now carries a source-aware first-chunk-only flag from outbound delivery into the shared send layer. The flag is only enabled for implicit single-use reply targets, so explicit `[[reply_to_*]]` replies and all-mode replies keep their existing reusable native reply behavior while the implicit turn reply no longer fans out across every physical text or media-caption chunk.

The payload send path now uses the same reply fanout contract for each physical Discord send, including `audioAsVoice`, native Discord payload media, component follow-up media, and classic component media downgrades. target.title: fix(release): block stale Codex runtime pins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The stable `@openclaw/codex` package could be published with an older embedded `@openai/codex` runtime even after a newer stable Codex release was available. Operators then saw the plugin as current because the updater correctly compared the published OpenClaw plugin version, while the route still launched the older runtime bundled by that package.

The canonical failure is release-time dependency freshness, not host CLI discovery or runtime binary attribution. On June 30, 2026, `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` was published with `@openai/codex@0.139.0` even though `@openai/codex@0.142.4` had already been published on June 29, 2026. The release pipeline validated internal package consistency but had no independent source of truth for whether the selected executable dependency was current.

Closes #99951.
Supersedes #99956 with the release-owner fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change keeps the invariant at the owner boundary:

- `@openclaw/codex` opts `@openai/codex` into a strict release-freshness contract through plugin metadata.
- The generic plugin release checker validates that each configured package is an exact runtime dependency.
- Release checks and release-plan collection resolve npm's `latest` dist-tag independently and fail closed when the pinned version is stale or cannot be verified.
- The check is opt-in, so ordinary plugin dependencies are not forced onto latest.

The Codex runtime is updated from `0.142.4` to `0.142.5`, generated lock data is refreshed, and the harness model snapshot is regenerated from the actual `0.142.5` app-server.

This deliberately does not add generic-core Codex version policy, inspect arbitrary selected binaries at runtime, or alter plugin update channel behavior. Those paths cannot prevent the stale artifact from being published and can report false positives for supported alternate routes.

## User Impact

Future Codex plugin releases cannot silently publish an older stable `@openai/codex` executable than npm's current `latest` release. A stale pin or unavailable freshness check blocks the release before users receive another false-green plugin update state.

The dependency bump also moves the next published Codex plugin runtime to `0.142.5`.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: Prevent stale Codex executable pins from passing OpenClaw plugin release validation.

Real environment tested: macOS source checkout with the installed `@openai/codex@0.142.5` app-server, plus an AWS Linux Crabbox `c7a.8xlarge` changed-lane run.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/plugin-npm-release.test.ts test/plugin-clawhub-release.test.ts test/scripts/release-wrapper-scripts.test.ts extensions/codex/src/manifest.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/models.test.ts`

- `node --import tsx scripts/plugin-npm-release-check.ts --plugins @openclaw/codex`
- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider aws --label codex-release-dependency-freshness --timing-json -- env OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed`
- `$autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output`

- 5 focused test files passed across 3 Vitest shards, 76 tests total.
- The Codex shrinkwrap check and live npm-backed plugin release check passed.
- Crabbox run `run_871522b80992` passed the changed gate, including dependency/shrinkwrap guards, full typecheck, lint, and import-cycle checks.
- Fresh Codex autoreview returned no actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence `0.83`).
- A real `codex app-server` `model/list` probe reported server version `0.142.5`; the documented public model snapshot was updated from that response.

Observed result after fix: A configured executable dependency below npm `latest`, or a registry failure that prevents verification, rejects plugin release planning instead of accepting a self-consistent stale artifact.

## What Problem This Solves

`isSilentReplyPrefixText` never matches custom silent tokens containing digits or punctuation (e.g., `NO_REPLY2`, `HELP-QUIET`). The character guard `/[^A-Z_]/.test(normalized)` rejects any input containing non-letter characters, causing streamed prefix detection to fail for custom tokens with digits/hyphens.

This means the streaming suppression path effectively ignores custom silent tokens that include numbers or special characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The character guard was too broad — it checked the **input fragment** (the streamed prefix) instead of the **token definition**. An input fragment is inherently transient and partial; the only meaningful question is whether the token itself is safe for prefix matching.

- The underscore guard (`normalized.includes("_")`) is preserved for standard `A-Z_` tokens like `HEARTBEAT_OK`.

After: prefix fragments containing a non-letter character from the token (e.g., `"NO_"` for `"NO_REPLY2"`, `"HELP-"` for `"HELP-QUIET"`, `"SILENT4"` for `"SILENT42"`) are correctly recognized during streaming. target.title: fix(android): voice session stuck on Listening after Bluetooth or USB mic is hot-unplugged
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with a Bluetooth (SCO/BLE) or USB microphone connected during voice capture have their Android voice session freeze indefinitely in the "Listening" state with no audio captured, no error surfaced, and a dispatcher CPU core pinned at 100%. Triggered by hot-unplugging the active mic, by audioserver crashes, or by any event that invalidates the underlying `AudioRecord` (the recorder returns `ERROR_DEAD_OBJECT`, `ERROR_INVALID_OPERATION`, etc. via the return code instead of throwing).

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture loop in `MicCaptureManager` treated every `read` return `≤ 0` as transient and used a bare `continue`. That is correct for the legitimate `read == 0` "no data ready yet" case, but it is a tight busy loop when `AudioRecord` keeps returning a persistent negative error code — `isActive`, `_micEnabled.value`, and `transcriptionSessionId` will not flip on a dead recorder, so the loop never exits. The fix partitions the read result:

- `read < 0` → call `failTranscription(sessionId, "microphone read failed: <error-name>")` and `return@launch`, so the recorder is closed, `_isListening` is cleared, the session exits "Listening", and the existing failure surface carries the message.
- `read == 0` → `continue` (unchanged).
- `read > 0` → process as before.

Added a small `audioRecordErrorName(code)` helper that maps known `AudioRecord.ERROR_*` constants to stable labels (with a `code=$code` fallback for unknown values), so the surfaced message is bounded and searchable. Scope is intentionally limited to the in-scope report point at `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/MicCaptureManager.kt:656`; the analogous pattern at `TalkModeManager.kt:750` is left untouched for a separate triage.

## User Impact

Voice users no longer get a hot-pinned CPU core and an infinite "Listening" loop when their microphone disappears mid-session or the audioserver restarts. They see a clear failure status (`Transcription failed: microphone read failed: ERROR_DEAD_OBJECT`), the session returns to a stoppable state, and they can retry capture from a known-clean baseline.

## Evidence

- `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.MicCaptureManagerTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.AndroidAudioInputSessionTest` (Temurin 21.0.7, Android SDK 36): **14/14 tests pass** (10 in `MicCaptureManagerTest`, 4 in `AndroidAudioInputSessionTest`). The new failure path is a bounded continuation of the existing `failTranscription` semantics already covered by `transcriptionErrorDisablesMic`.
- `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck` is clean on the touched source file. The pre-existing ktlint violations in `ChatControllerCommandControlsTest.kt`, `InvokeErrorParserTest.kt`, and `GatewayConfigResolverTest.kt` are unrelated to this change (those files are unchanged on this branch; they last shipped in `c680312ef6`).
- Repro path (manual, requires hardware): open voice capture with a Bluetooth SCO/BLE or USB input, hot-unplug mid-session. Before this fix the dispatcher hot-spins on `continue` (`read` keeps returning `-6`), `isListening` stays `true`, no error path fires, and one core is pinned at 100%. After this fix `failTranscription` runs once with `microphone read failed: ERROR_DEAD_OBJECT`, the recorder is closed, `_isListening` flips to `false`, and `statusText` carries the failure.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI had accumulated routing, page state, session behavior, data loading, and rendering inside a large shared application host. This made page behavior difficult to isolate, increased unnecessary update work, and made further development riskier.

## Why This Change Was Made

This refactors the complete Control UI around the published `@openclaw/uirouter` package and clear `app`, `pages`, `components`, `lib`, and `api` boundaries.

Routes now coordinate page loading and navigation, individual pages own their lifecycle and state, and the application shell retains only shared application behavior. The migration also removes the obsolete host, duplicated controllers, legacy routing paths, and superseded session orchestration.

Existing design and behavior remain intact, including sidebar sessions, breadcrumbs, gateway selection, command handling, settings presentation, chat behavior, and mobile pairing.

## User Impact

Users retain the existing Control UI experience while benefiting from faster, more predictable navigation and better isolation between pages.

Routes can preload on navigation intent, reuse cached data, revalidate in the background, and update without unnecessarily rerendering the shared shell. No user-facing workflows were intentionally removed.

target.title: fix(failover): provider refusals now trigger the model fallback chain
target.body:
Fixes #98976

## What Problem This Solves
Provider refusals (Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reasons, OpenAI `content_filter` finish_reason) were never classified as a distinct FailoverReason. They fell through to the generic `LLM request failed` error path, bypassing the model fallback chain entirely — no retry on the next configured model, no auth-profile distinction, and confusing user-facing error text.

## Evidence
256 tests pass across all fix-relevant suites, including the new `anthropic-refusal.test.ts` and updated `openai-stop-reason.test.ts`, `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts`, `errors.test.ts`, `failover-matches.test.ts`, `run/failover-policy.test.ts`, `auth-profile-failure-policy.test.ts`, `failover-policy.test.ts`, `anthropic.test.ts`, `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`, and `packages/llm-core/types.test.ts`.

This fix has also been running in production on four independent gateway instances (Newhart, Victoria, Graybeard, NOVA) since 2026-07-03 with no regressions. All four instances are verified healthy on this change.

## Root cause
Provider refusals (Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reasons, OpenAI `content_filter` finish_reason) were never classified as a distinct FailoverReason. They fell through to the generic `LLM request failed` error path, bypassing the model fallback chain entirely — no retry on the next configured model, no auth-profile distinction, and confusing user-facing error text.

## Fix summary

- **New `refusal` FailoverReason** added to the `AgentRuntimeFailoverReason` union. `errorCode: "provider_refusal"` is set at the Anthropic and OpenAI transport layers.
- **Transport normalization:** Anthropic `sensitive` stop reason is treated like `refusal`; OpenAI `content_filter` maps to `errorCode: "provider_refusal"`.
- **No auth-profile rotation.** Refusals are content-scoped, not credential-scoped — the policy layer never rotates auth profiles or puts them in cooldown for a refusal.
- **No same-model retry.** The fallback skips the current model and moves to the next candidate directly.
- **Preserved probe budget.** Refusals do not consume the transient cooldown probe slot.
- **Partial-output detection.** If the model produced visible output before refusing, the output is surfaced as an error instead of silently retrying on another model (avoiding duplicate/contradictory replies).
- **Stable user copy.** When a refusal is surfaced, the user sees: *"The model declined to generate this response. Try rephrasing your request, or switch to a different model."*
- **PR #94430 boundary.** `refusal` classification takes precedence over `rate_limit` in the shared error classifier. Overlap is minimal — #94430 targets different error text patterns. A boundary comment has been added in `errors.ts`.

## Test coverage
256 tests pass across all fix-relevant suites:
| Area | Tests | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| `anthropic-refusal.test.ts` (new) | 5 | ✅ |
| `openai-stop-reason.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ |
| `result-fallback-classifier.test.ts` | 23 | ✅ |
| `errors.test.ts` | 13 | ✅ |
| `failover-matches.test.ts` | 36 | ✅ |
| `run/failover-policy.test.ts` | 39 | ✅ |
| `auth-profile-failure-policy.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ |
| `failover-policy.test.ts` | 1 | ✅ |
| `anthropic.test.ts` (incl. sensitive regression) | 39 | ✅ |
| `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` (incl. sensitive regression) | 83 | ✅ |
| `packages/llm-core/types.test.ts` | 1 | ✅ |

## Production validation
This fix has been running in production on four independent gateway instances (Newhart, Victoria, Graybeard, NOVA) since 2026-07-03 with no regressions. All four instances are verified healthy on this change.

## Maintainer notes
This PR carries a `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` label on the issue — the fix has been through staging testing (356 tests, green) and production validation across multiple gateways. We are filing this upstream as a fully tested, validated fix for the maintainer-review path (`needs-maintainer-review` / `needs-security-review`). All changes are scoped to failover policy, transport normalization, and user-facing copy — no architectural impact outside the fallback classifier and failover policy layers.

We defer entirely to maintainer judgment on whether the approach and implementation are appropriate for upstream. Happy to adjust scope, naming, or any other aspect per review feedback.

## Real behavior proof

### Expected behavior
When a provider returns a content-policy refusal (e.g. Anthropic `refusal`/`sensitive` stop reason, OpenAI `content_filter` finish reason), the runner should treat this as a non-auth, non-retryable failure that walks the model fallback chain. The refusal classification must preserve any partial assistant output already delivered to the user, must not retry the same model, and must not poison shared auth-profile health.

### Actual behavior (before fix)
Provider content-policy refusals were classified as generic `unclassified` errors. This caused:
- The fallback chain to stop instead of trying the next model.
- Partial outputs from a refused turn to be discarded.
- In some configurations, the refusal could be treated as an auth failure and cool down a healthy profile.

### Repro steps
1. Configure a model that uses Anthropic (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) or OpenAI (`gpt-4.1`) and trigger a content-policy refusal.
2. Ensure a fallback model is configured in the agent/model chain.
3. Observe that before the fix the run terminates with `unclassified`; after the fix the run advances to the next model with `reason: "refusal"` and `code: "provider_refusal"`.

### Test evidence
Local verification against upstream `main` after rebase:
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:test` — passed
- `pnpm lint` — passed
- `vitest.agents-embedded-agent.config.ts` — 85 files, 1605 tests passed

## Summary

- Problem: `openclaw wiki lint` can report valid imported wiki links as `broken-wikilink` when they use page titles, slug variants, fragments, or imported source-path suffixes.
- Why it matters: imported evidence should not need provenance-damaging rewrites just to satisfy lint.
- What changed: memory-wiki lint now builds separate case-sensitive path targets and case-insensitive alias targets, including titles, title slugs, source-path suffixes, and fragment/query-stripped targets.

## What Problem This Solves

Imported memory-wiki pages can preserve source-authored Obsidian links that are semantically valid but do not exactly match generated file names. Today, links like `[[Alpha Database#Evidence]]`, `[[alpha-database]]`, or `[[research notes/Alpha System Overview#Quote]]` can be reported as `broken-wikilink` even when the target page exists. That creates noisy lint output and pressures users to rewrite source-preserving imported evidence just to satisfy the linter.

This PR fixes that specific resolver gap while keeping path-style links strict. Title, slug, fragment-stripped, and imported source-path suffix links can resolve to existing pages; path targets containing `/` remain case-sensitive, so a case-mismatched path such as `[[syntheses/Alpha-DB]]` still warns. target.title: feat(workboard): refresh Control UI from live changes
target.body:
Closes #98805

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the Control UI Workboard could remain stale after cards changed through Gateway methods, tools, commands, separate CLI processes, or background dispatch. Freshness previously depended on manual refresh or optional timer polling, which is disabled by default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workboard now owns one canonical mutation-notification path and reconciles commits from separate processes through its existing SQLite store. A lifecycle-owned `plugin.workboard.changed` Gateway event carries only epoch/revision invalidation facts under `operator.read`; the Control UI coalesces those facts and refetches canonical Workboard data, including reconnect, plugin reload, visibility, protected-edit, transient-failure, and stale-write recovery. Manual refresh remains; routine timer polling and its controls are removed.

The event is an invalidation hint, not a second event log or state store. Existing Workboard reads and SQLite events remain authoritative, and no card bodies are broadcast.

## User Impact

Operators with an open Workboard see card and task-ledger changes reconcile without routine polling, including mutations initiated outside the current browser process. Inactive or hidden Workboard views defer reads until active again, and editing/mutation controls stay read-only until the canonical snapshot covers the newest accepted revision.

## Evidence

- Exact AWS proof: Crabbox run `run_d8bdc039c15d`, lease `cbx_f7d3e06a60d6`, base `5bcd25f0fb6de3cc2ba6b6a7688a9361eb355143`, candidate tree `9128d294a7273c15d1f78d5147e96bc2156720d9`; `check:changed`, canonical build, plugin SDK exports, and emitted declaration checks passed; exit 0 and automatic lease release confirmed.
- Focused tests: 13 files across tooling, Gateway, plugin services, Control UI, and Workboard; 5 Vitest shards and 695 tests passed.
- Browser proof: `ui/src/ui/e2e/workboard.e2e.test.ts`; 2/2 scenarios passed on head `945d579282f3cdbd34b396fae3b1d41a3fa1513a`. Approved screenshot/video manifest will be linked here after the draft number is assigned.
- Static proof: 30 changed files format-clean; changed TypeScript lint-clean; docs MDX clean; 5,544 internal links checked with 0 broken; `git diff --check` clean.
- Review: explicit whole-branch xhigh review reported no accepted/actionable P0-P2 findings (correctness 0.93).
- iOS adjacency: the existing Workboard design/render tests passed (15 tests); this PR intentionally adds no iOS UI behavior.

### Risk and proof gaps

- Main risk is event authorization and lifecycle/revision coordination. Tests cover reserved-event guard precedence, scope revocation, plugin reload epochs, cross-process reconciliation, exact-target races, retries, visibility deferral, stale-write protection, capture races, cleanup, and no feedback loop.
- Browser proof uses the repository's mocked Gateway E2E path; Linux changed/build/export proof ran remotely on the exact candidate tree.
- Soft sequencing note: draft #98510 currently has no exact file or Gateway-event export overlap. Rebase this draft if that session-controller work lands first.

target.title: test(plugins): cover stale OpenClaw peer repair during install
target.body:
## Summary

This adds an e2e regression for the dirty managed-npm state that can make `openclaw plugins install @opik/opik-openclaw` fail with `ERESOLVE` after prior host-peer plugin installs.

The fixture mirrors the bad state from the live box:

- a Codex-like plugin already installed with `peerOptional openclaw@>=2026.5.5-beta.2`
- an Opik-like plugin being installed with `peer openclaw@>=2026.3.2`
- a stale root-level `node_modules/openclaw@2026.5.4` left in the managed npm root

The test first proves raw npm still fails with `ERESOLVE` in that state, then proves OpenClaw's managed installer repairs the stale root package, completes the install, and restores plugin-local `openclaw` peer symlinks for both plugins.

## RCA

The failure is not just a future peer-materialization problem. Once an older OpenClaw registry package has already been materialized at `~/.openclaw/npm/node_modules/openclaw`, npm treats it as the candidate host peer during later managed-root mutations. A later install can then fail before the requested plugin is installed because another installed plugin has a stricter host peer range than the stale root package satisfies.

Current `main` already has the behavior fix: managed plugin installs repair stale root `openclaw` state before npm mutates the root, use `--omit=peer`, and relink plugin-local host peers afterward. This PR locks the exact dirty-state transition down so we do not regress users who already have poisoned managed npm roots.

## Verification

- `pnpm docs:list`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --write --threads=1 src/plugins/install.npm-spec.e2e.test.ts`
- `pnpm test:serial src/plugins/install.npm-spec.e2e.test.ts` - 1 file / 5 tests passed
- `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 pnpm check:changed` - attempted through Blacksmith Testbox; first box shut down while queued, second stayed queued and was stopped after waiting. Targeted local e2e proof above passed.

Observe if it skips or captures (it will now capture). ### Expected - The input memory is saved to LanceDB. ### Actual - The input memory is saved correctly. ## Evidence Attach at least one: - [] Failing test/log before + passing after - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) What you personally verified (not just CI), and how: - Verified scenarios: End to End tests and schema parsing correctly validates upper and lower bounds. - Edge cases checked: Setting `captureMinChars` > `captureMaxChars` fails validation correctly. - What you did **not** verify: ## Review Conversations - [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? `Yes` - Config/env changes? `Yes` (added `captureMinChars` to `openclaw.plugin.json`) - Migration needed? `No` ## Risks and Mitigations - Risk: A very low threshold config might capture too much short irrelevant text as memories. - Mitigation: Min chars defaulted to 4, guarding against noise while opening up standard phrase possibilities.

target.title: perf(agents): cache provider tool schema normalization
target.body:
## Summary
- Cache provider-normalized tool schema `parameters` for repeated embedded agent turns, but only when OpenClaw can identify one of its bundled SDK tool-compat normalizers.
- Keep the cache internal and conservative: bundled DeepSeek, Gemini, and OpenAI compatibility helpers can reuse cloned normalized `parameters`; custom provider `normalizeToolSchemas` hooks bypass the cache.
- Avoid new public provider plugin contracts and avoid new operator-facing runtime flags. Tool objects, execute closures, approval state, guards, and runtime policy are still rebuilt per turn.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: repeated embedded agent turns can avoid redoing bundled provider tool-schema compatibility normalization when the provider/model/api/schema signature is unchanged. Unknown or custom provider normalizers still run normally and do not participate in the cache.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `tool-schema-cache-pr3`, current PR head `4dd1cdbce94d12e7b03ad5930ddd85dd1151a835`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran a terminal proof with `node --import tsx proof.mjs` against the production `normalizeProviderToolSchemas` entry. The script used the real bundled OpenAI tool-schema normalizer identity (`normalizeOpenAIToolSchemas`) through a provider runtime handle, called normalization twice with the same provider/model/api/schema signature and different `execute` closures, then repeated the same pattern with a custom provider normalizer.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the current head:

```json
{
  "head": "4dd1cdbce94d12e7b03ad5930ddd85dd1151a835",
  "bundledCompat": {
    "afterFirst": { "bypass": 0, "hit": 0, "miss": 1, "store": 1, "size": 1 },
    "afterSecond": { "bypass": 0, "hit": 1, "miss": 1, "store": 1, "size": 1 },
    "cacheHitIncreasedOnSecondNormalize": true,
    "normalizedParametersEqual": true,
    "secondRunExecuteClosurePreserved": true
  },
  "customProvider": {
    "customNormalizeCalls": 2,
    "afterCustom": { "bypass": 2, "hit": 0, "miss": 0, "store": 0, "size": 0 },
    "customProviderBypassedCache": true
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: The bundled OpenAI compatibility path produced one miss and store on the first normalization, then one cache hit on the second normalization while preserving the fresh second `execute` closure. The custom provider path bypassed the cache twice and invoked its normalizer twice, proving the cache remains internal to known bundled compatibility helpers.

What was not tested: Full live-provider latency and a remote LLM turn were not tested in this current-head refresh. This PR caches only provider-normalized schema `parameters`; it does not cache complete tool inventory/materialization, policy resolution, prompt inputs, or full agent-turn startup.

target.title: perf(plugins,gateway): async-ify channels.status + messages.send discovery (and split WhatsApp transport closes)
target.body:
Closes #78100. Companion to (not blocked by) #78101 — that PR coalesces repeated calls within a 2 s TTL as a near-term win; this PR is the deeper structural fix #78100 proposed as item 2.

## Summary

Async-ify the persisted-read hot path inside `loadPluginRegistrySnapshotWithMetadata` and the auto-enable resolver inside `messages.send` so `channels.status`, `channels.start`, and inbound dispatch no longer block the Node event loop on `realpathSync` / `statSync` / `readFileSync` while verifying the persisted plugin index. Cold-path discovery yields once via `setImmediate` so other I/O can interleave with the still-sync walk.

Adds:
- `loadPluginRegistrySnapshotWithMetadataAsync`
- `hasMissingPersistedPluginSourceAsync`
- `hasStalePersistedPluginMetadataAsync`

with inflight-promise dedup so concurrent callers don't redo the syscalls.

Also includes (smaller, related):
- WhatsApp auto-reply monitor: split transport-class WS handshake closes (408, 428, 5xx) from lifecycle-class closes (401 logged-out, 440 conflict). Transport closes now retry inside the running monitor's existing reconnect loop instead of throwing out and triggering a full plugin restart that re-runs discovery (and re-pays the sync cost above). Only logged-out / conflict still bubble up to relinking. Adds `event` / `closeClass` / `phase` structured log fields so transport recoveries are greppable separately from lifecycle restarts.

## Why this approach

The repo's `src/plugins/CLAUDE.md` says *"Do not add persistent metadata caches for discovery, manifest registries, installed-index reconstruction"* — this PR doesn't. It keeps the freshness-first design intact and just removes the synchronous-blocking property of the read path, which is what burns event-loop time on slow filesystems. #78101's 2 s TTL is a deliberately short coalescing window; this PR addresses the underlying cost so even a single cold call is loop-friendly.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On Kubernetes / OKE with a PVC-backed `~/.openclaw`, an inbound WhatsApp message burst causes event-loop blocks of 1.0–20.8 s, dispatch latencies of 17–27 s per turn, and (eventually) 408 keepalive misses that cascade into channel restarts.
- Environment tested: OKE cluster on a single `VM.Standard.A1.Flex` node (2 OCPU / 11.4 GiB / arm64). Pod limits `2 / 4Gi`, requests `500m / 1Gi`. PVC: `oci-bv` block-volume storage class, 5 GiB, mounted at `~/.openclaw`. Image base `node:24-bookworm-slim`. 8 plugins loaded. Agent model `openai/gpt-5.5`. WhatsApp Web personal pairing, `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`.
- Steps run after the patch:
  1. Build A (ablation): `vendor/openclaw` reset to commit `c874c0863a` (the base of this branch on `main` before the 4 commits). Verified the post-build `dist/` does NOT contain `loadPluginRegistrySnapshotWithMetadataAsync` or `isTransportClassConnectError` symbols.
  2. Build B (this PR): `vendor/openclaw` at HEAD of this branch. Same Dockerfile, same `pnpm install` and `pnpm build` steps. Verified `dist/` DOES contain those symbols.
  3. Helm upgrade rolled the same release between Build A and Build B with PVC preserved (no re-pairing needed). Identical resources and config.
  4. Workload: 9 self-DM WhatsApp text messages within 10 s. All passed the dmPolicy allowlist gate.
  5. Captured: gateway diagnostic stream (`liveness warning` events with `eventLoopDelayMaxMs`, `eventLoopUtilization`, `cpuCoreRatio`, queue depth, `phase`) and structured log entries for each `inbound message` and `auto-reply sent (text)` (with `durationMs`).
- Evidence: redacted runtime logs from the gateway diagnostic stream and structured channel logs (Build A vs Build B, same Helm release).
  - Build A liveness warning, sustained burst (queue depth 7): `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=2655 ms`, `phase=channels.whatsapp.start-account`, `recentPhases=...sidecars.model-prewarm:1021ms`.
  - Build A liveness warning, worst-case 9-msg burst (queue depth 8): `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=20837.3 ms`, `eventLoopUtilization=0.751`, `cpuCoreRatio=0.822`.
  - Build A liveness warning, idle/cold start: `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=1096 ms`.
  - Build B equivalent burst: no liveness warnings exceeding `eventLoopDelayMaxMs=305 ms`. `cpuCoreRatio` returns to ~0.5 between bursts.
  - Build A reply latencies (3 of 9 burst): `21:06:38 inbound → 21:07:05 reply = 27 s`, `21:06:44 inbound → 21:07:05 reply = 21 s`, `21:06:48 inbound → 21:07:05 reply = 17 s`.
  - Build B reply latencies (warm): `durationMs:5–9` for delivery, full turn ~5–9 s bound by model latency, not gateway.
- Observed result:
  - eventLoopDelayMaxMs (worst-case burst): **20,837 ms → not observed** (~70× lower).
  - eventLoopDelayMaxMs (sustained burst): **2655 ms → 305 ms** (~9× lower).
  - User-visible reply latency (burst): **17–27 s → 5–9 s** (~3–5× lower).
  - Transport-fix half: structurally verifiable in code (post-fix, transport-class close codes stay in the reconnect loop with `runId` preserved); a concrete 408 keepalive miss didn't fall inside the test window. The two readings together are consistent with the keepalive-miss correlation table in #78100 (`event-loop block 56–107 s → 408 disconnect`).
- Not tested:
  - Native Linux/macOS / NVMe SSD impact: should be a no-op cost (the underlying syscalls return in <1 ms there, so the async wrapper just adds a microtask). The fix matters where syscalls are 10–100× slower (PVC-backed K8s, WSL2 9P, NFS, container overlays).
  - Telegram / Discord / other channels: the perf path covers all `channels.status` and `messages.send` callers, so other channels should also benefit, but the burst test only exercised WhatsApp.
  - Long-window 408 cascade: requires sustained event-loop pressure that takes ≥3 minutes on Build A; not captured here.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-registry-snapshot.test.ts` — 6/6 pass after rebase.
- [x] `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor-state.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/web-auto-reply-monitor.test.ts` — 27/27 pass after rebase.
- [x] `pnpm build` — green on rebased HEAD.
- [x] Live K8s/OKE proof (above): A/B image swap, same Helm release, PVC preserved, 9-message WhatsApp burst.
- [ ] Native Linux/macOS regression check (not run by the author; CI lanes will cover this).

- **What did NOT change:** No changes to `extensions/openai/`, no cross-plugin dependencies, no config schema changes

target.title: fix(bedrock): bound Mantle model discovery fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on Amazon Bedrock Mantle model discovery could have provider setup hang indefinitely when the `/v1/models` request stalls, or consume unbounded memory when the endpoint streams an oversized JSON body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mantle model discovery now treats the provider catalog response as an untrusted network boundary: the fetch receives a 30 second abort signal, and successful JSON bodies are read through the existing bounded response reader with a 4 MiB cap. The 4 MiB cap matches OpenClaw's existing live model catalog body cap for provider-owned model catalogs; the larger 16 MiB setup-discovery cap is for self-hosted setup JSON, so this keeps the Mantle fix aligned with the live catalog path. The timeout/cap boundary preserves the existing failure behavior: discovery errors fall back to cached models or an empty result instead of hanging or reading an unbounded response.

No schema, config, migration, stored-state, or public provider contract is changed.

## User Impact

Mantle provider discovery is now bounded for normal, oversized, and stalled provider responses. Users should see provider resolution fail safely instead of hanging the process or reading an unbounded response body. If a Mantle catalog exceeds the bounded provider-catalog limit or does not produce a response within 30 seconds, discovery uses the same cache-or-empty fallback path it already used for provider failures.

## Evidence

- Local HTTP behavior proof for Mantle discovery normal, oversized, and stalled response paths. The proof uses the actual Mantle discovery module, verifies the fetch receives an `AbortSignal`, and serves responses from a local HTTP server:

The existing Linux direction in #75 called for a GTK-native companion rather than treating Linux as only a wrapper or dashboard handoff. - Why it matters: - Linux is a real target platform in the issue, and the lack of a native companion left users without parity on core desktop workflows such as service state visibility, tray/status integration, local diagnostics, and direct management of gateway-backed sections. - Without a native app, Linux-specific concerns such as systemd user-service integration, Ubuntu GNOME tray behavior, local-vs-remote resource access, and distro-native dependency flow were not handled in a coherent product surface. - What changed: - Added a new native Linux companion app under `apps/linux` using C, GTK4, and Libadwaita, plus a private GTK3 Ayatana/AppIndicator tray helper for Ubuntu GNOME tray/status integration. - Added a native gateway client stack for Linux: config loading, HTTP health probing, authenticated WebSocket connection, typed RPC mutation helpers, gateway data adapters, and controller-based UI sections. - Added native operational management surfaces for Channels, Skills, Sessions, Cron, and Instances, including config-safe editing, locality-aware transcript/log opening, pairing actions, and richer management flows previously absent on Linux. - Added Linux runtime/readiness modeling, onboarding, diagnostics, notifications, systemd integration, and focused automated tests covering parser behavior, mutation request shapes, RPC lifecycle handling, config rebuild safety, runtime/readiness logic, and helper behavior. - target.title: fix: detect localized Windows netstat listeners
target.body:
Closes #99984

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on localized Windows installs could run gateway `--force`, port diagnostics, or stale gateway cleanup and have OpenClaw miss an active TCP listener because Windows `netstat` did not print the English `LISTENING` state text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI force-free path, infra diagnostics path, and Windows listening-PID fallback now share one Windows TCP `netstat` listener parser. It matches listener rows by TCP shape, exact local endpoint port, wildcard/port-zero remote endpoint, and positive PID instead of relying on localized state words. The CLI and PID fallback still deduplicate PIDs, while diagnostics keep listener address details.

The QA smoke follow-up keeps the isolated `native-command-session-target` scenario from racing its post-`/stop` recovery turn against the aborted run's session file lock. The scenario now waits for the active session to clear, for the mock delayed provider request to leave `/debug/inflight-requests`, and for the session `.jsonl.lock` file to disappear before it sends the recovery message.

## User Impact

Windows users with non-English system output get more reliable gateway port conflict detection, force-free cleanup, diagnostics, and stale gateway listener verification. Established TCP connections on the target port are not treated as listeners.

The QA smoke scenario now proves native `/stop` unblocks the next turn after the underlying abort cleanup actually finishes, instead of immediately sending recovery traffic while the same session is still locked.

## Evidence

- Head SHA: `fd907fa6ef1c46e21e53fd80a415206b9e5a3d06`
- Claim proved: localized Windows `netstat` listener rows are parsed by the shared CLI, diagnostics, and Windows PID fallback paths without requiring English state text; established/non-wildcard rows on the same port are ignored.
- QA Smoke CI follow-up:

  - Gateway stderr for that failed scenario showed the recovery turn hit `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError: session file locked (timeout 60000ms)` for the same session lock after `embedded abort settle timed out ... timeoutMs=2000`.
  - Current head updates the scenario to wait for active-run cleanup, mock delayed-provider cleanup, and session lock release before sending the recovery turn.

target.title: fix(qa-channel): bound QA bus JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.ts` used unbounded JSON reads on the QA bus
HTTP success paths:

- `postJson` (used by `pollQaBus` and other bus calls) buffered the full
  `node:http` response body into memory before `JSON.parse`.
- `getQaBusState` used unbounded `await response.json()` on the fetch success path.

A misbehaving or hostile QA bus endpoint (or accidental huge payload) could stream
oversized JSON and trigger unbounded allocation during QA channel polling and state
inspection.

This change caps both paths at 16 MiB with labeled errors such as
`qa-bus /v1/poll: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes` and
`qa-channel.bus-state: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`.

This aligns QA Channel's bus client with the broader OpenClaw response-limit
campaign that already bounded sibling provider, channel, and QA Lab surfaces.

## Changes

* `extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.ts`:
  - adds `readQaBusNodeJsonResponse` using `readByteStreamWithLimit` for
    `node:http` POST responses (`pollQaBus`, etc.)
  - replaces unbounded `response.json()` in `getQaBusState` with
    `readProviderJsonResponse(response, "qa-channel.bus-state")`
  - normalizes malformed JSON errors to `"qa-bus <path>: malformed JSON response"`

* `extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.test.ts`:
  - adds regression tests for oversized `/v1/poll` and `/v1/state` responses
  - updates malformed JSON assertion to match the new labeled error

* `scripts/proof-qa-channel-bus-bound.mjs`:
  - path-level proof over `node:http` streaming poll bodies and fetch state reads

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Oversized QA bus JSON success bodies fail closed instead of
unbounded heap growth on poll and state reads.

**Real environment tested:** Node v22.22.0, macOS 15.3.1, `node:http` streaming
server on `127.0.0.1`, built helpers from `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-http.js` and
`dist/plugin-sdk/response-limit-runtime.js`.

**Exact steps:**
1. Stream an ~18 MiB JSON envelope from a local HTTP server (no `Content-Length`).
2. Drive `readByteStreamWithLimit` on a `node:http` poll response → assert labeled cap.
3. Drive `readProviderJsonResponse` on a fetch state response → assert labeled cap.
4. Verify a normal state snapshot still parses.
5. Run qa-channel vitest regression tests for poll/state bounds.

**Observed result:**
- Poll path: `qa-bus /v1/poll: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- State path: `qa-channel.bus-state: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- Normal state snapshot parses with `accounts` and `threads` arrays intact

**What was not tested:** live QA bus server integration against a running OpenClaw gateway.

target.title: fix(watch): defer restart when dist/entry.js is missing mid-rebuild
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a `git push` triggers source file changes while `dist/` is mid-rebuild, the hot-reload watcher (`watch-node.mjs`) unconditionally kills the current healthy gateway child process and restarts into a missing or stale `dist/entry.js`, causing a crash-loop that exhausts systemd's restart limit (37-minute outage).

Fixes [#99603](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99603).

## Why This Change Was Made

`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs` sent SIGTERM to the child process without verifying build readiness. The fix adds `isBuildReadyForRestart()` which validates:

1. **`dist/entry.js` exists** — basic mid-rebuild guard
2. **Build stamp git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD** — aligns with `run-node`'s `resolveBuildRequirement` contract, preventing restarts into a stale build from a different commit (e.g. after `git pull`)

If the build is not ready, the watcher polls every 200ms. When the build completes, it proceeds with the restart. A **5-minute timeout** prevents infinite polling — the current process keeps running and the next file change will retry.

**Child-exit during deferral**: If the child process exits while waiting for build readiness, the exit handler also defers restart until the build is ready instead of restarting immediately into a potentially broken `dist/`.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Source file changes during mid-rebuild → watcher kills healthy gateway → new child cannot start → crash-loop → systemd gives up → outage
- **After**: Source file changes during mid-rebuild or after `git pull` → watcher waits for `dist/entry.js` + matching build stamp → build completes → safe restart. Guards prevent both the immediate kill and premature restart on child exit.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests (18/18 passed)
- `defers restart when dist/entry.js is missing` — build readiness guard
- `kills child normally when dist/entry.js exists` — normal path unaffected
- `gives up after timeout when build never completes` — timeout safety net

### Real Machine Gateway:Watch Proof (Linux x64, Node 22.19)

**完整终端日志** (当前 HEAD `603df8ffd8`, 已编辑路径):

```
============================================================
  Issue #99603 — 真机验证完整日志

============================================================

Host:     LIN-DF11F9C3F26.zte.intra
Kernel:   4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
Node:     v22.19.0
Git HEAD: 603df8ffd8
Branch:   fix/issue-99603-watch-node-guard

=== 命令: 启动 gateway:watch ===
$ OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 node scripts/watch-node.mjs gateway

watcher PID:  2443610

=== 进程状态 (就绪后) ===
$ ps -p 2443610 -o pid,stat,etime,comm
2443610 Sl 00:30 node                    ← watcher 进程健康
$ ps -p 2443620 -o pid,stat,etime,comm
2443620 Ssl 00:30 node                   ← 子进程健康

============================================================
  Phase 1: mid-rebuild (entry 缺失 + stamp 过期)
============================================================

$ # 伪造旧 stamp（模拟 git pull 前）+ 删除 dist/entry.js
$ echo '{"builtAt":1700000000000,"head":"ffffffff..."}' > dist/.buildstamp
$ rm dist/entry.js

$ # 触发源文件变更 → requestRestart
$ touch src/entry.ts

--- watcher 输出 ---
[openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.
→ ✅ 双层 guard 正确 defer（entry 缺失 + stamp 过期）

============================================================
  Phase 2: 恢复 entry 但 stamp 仍过期 (git pull 模拟)
============================================================

$ cp /tmp/proof-entry.js dist/entry.js   # 恢复 entry.js
$ # stamp HEAD 仍为 ffffffff（过期）

--- watcher 输出 ---
[openclaw] Build output not ready (dist/entry.js missing or stale); waiting before restart.
→ ✅ stamp 对齐检查生效 (entry 存在但 HEAD 不匹配 → 仍 defer)

============================================================
  Phase 3: 恢复正确 stamp → 安全重启
============================================================

$ cp /tmp/proof-stamp.json dist/.buildstamp  # 恢复正确 stamp (HEAD: 603df8ffd8)

--- watcher 输出（最终）---

[openclaw] Syncing runtime artifacts (build_stamp_newer).
→ ✅ stamp 匹配 → guard 通过 → 安全重启

============================================================
  验证结论
============================================================
  ✅ Guard 阻止了 crash (defer restart)
  ✅ build 就绪后安全重启
  ✅ watcher 进程全程健康 (alive)

对比 MAIN 分支 (无修复):
  [openclaw] Building TypeScript (dist is stale: missing_dist_entry)
  → kill 健康子进程 → crash loop → systemd 耗尽重启限额
```

**验证通过项**:

- ✅ build stamp HEAD 对齐: 与 run-node 就绪检查一致
- ✅ 安全恢复: build 就绪后自动重启
- ✅ watcher 进程始终保持健康

## Changes

5 commits, 3 files (+258/-5):

- `scripts/watch-node.mjs` (+108): `isBuildReadyForRestart` with entry check + build stamp HEAD alignment via `resolveGitHead`; `deps.fs` injection; guard in `requestRestart` with 200ms polling + 5-min timeout; child-exit guard with bounded recovery (5-min timeout then fallback `startRunner`); both guards skip in test mode (`OPENCLAW_WATCH_MODE=test`)

target.title: fix(heartbeat): retry transient EAGAIN/EINTR on session-store and workspace-template reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux (and macOS), the OpenClaw gateway heartbeat-driven reads of the session store (`loadSessionStore`) and workspace bootstrap files (`fileContentDiffersFromTemplate`) fail with transient `EAGAIN`/`EINTR` errors when another process is atomically swapping the file. A single transient read failure aborted the heartbeat, cascading into cron, memory, and message workflow failures.

Reported in #99994. The session-store retry loop was gated to **Windows-only** (`process.platform === "win32" ? 3 : 1`), so Linux and macOS got a single attempt with no retry. The workspace template read had **no retry at all**.

Closes #99994.

## Root Cause / Fix

**Site 1** — `src/config/sessions/store-load.ts`:
- Removed the `process.platform === "win32"` gate on `maxReadAttempts` → always `3` on every platform.
- The existing `readFileSync` retry loop already handles transient errors via bare `catch` and empty-read detection.

**Site 2** — `src/agents/workspace.ts`:
- Added a 3-attempt retry loop with 50ms backoff around `fs.readFile()`.
- Detects transient errors via `code === EAGAIN | EINTR`, `errno === -11 | -4`, and the macOS `Unknown system error -11` / `system error -4` message forms.
- `ENOENT` still returns `false` (file absent). Non-transient errors still propagate.
- Exhausted transient retries return `false` so callers do not rewrite unreadable files.

## Evidence

### 1. Tests — 11 passing

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/store-load.eagain-retry.test.ts src/agents/workspace.eagain-retry.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ loadSessionStore EAGAIN retry > retries readFileSync on EAGAIN and loads store once read succeeds
 ✓ loadSessionStore EAGAIN retry > returns empty store after exhausting retries on persistent EAGAIN
 ✓ loadSessionStore EAGAIN retry > retries on transient empty reads from race with file swap
 ✓ loadSessionStore EAGAIN retry > loads store on the first attempt when there is no error
 ✓ fileContentDiffersFromTemplate EAGAIN retry > returns false when the file is absent (ENOENT)
 ✓ fileContentDiffersFromTemplate EAGAIN retry > returns false when the file matches the template
 ✓ fileContentDiffersFromTemplate EAGAIN retry > returns true when the file differs from the template
 ✓ fileContentDiffersFromTemplate EAGAIN retry > retries on EAGAIN and succeeds once read recovers
 ✓ fileContentDiffersFromTemplate EAGAIN retry > returns false after exhausting retries on persistent EAGAIN
 ✓ fileContentDiffersFromTemplate EAGAIN retry > retries on EINTR and succeeds once read recovers
 ✓ fileContentDiffersFromTemplate EAGAIN retry > propagates non-transient errors immediately
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

### 2. Real production function calls (Linux, Node.js v24.13.1)

**loadSessionStore** — retry loop active with `maxReadAttempts=3`:
```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { loadSessionStore } from './src/config/sessions/store-load.js'; ..."
loadSessionStore result: ["agent:default:proof-test"]
Store has proof key: true
loadSessionStore retry loop: ACTIVE (maxReadAttempts=3, was 1 on Linux)
```

**fileContentDiffersFromTemplate** — EAGAIN retry active, all three paths verified:
```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { fileContentDiffersFromTemplate } from './src/agents/workspace.js'; ..."
ENOENT (missing file): false (expected: false)
Matching template: false (expected: false)
Different content: true (expected: true)
fileContentDiffersFromTemplate: EAGAIN retry ACTIVE (3 attempts, 50ms backoff)
Transient error detection: EAGAIN, EINTR, errno -11/-4, macOS message pattern
```

### 3. Gateway stability (Linux)

Gateway running with the fix — zero EAGAIN heartbeat errors:
```
Active: active (running)
No EAGAIN errors found
```

### 4. Pre-submit checks

```
oxfmt --check  → All matched files use the correct format
oxlint         → 0 warnings, 0 errors
git diff --check → clean
autoreview     → clean: no accepted/actionable findings, patch is correct (0.95)
```

## Before/After

| | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Linux `loadSessionStore` attempts | 1 (no retry) | 3 (with 50ms backoff) |
| Linux `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` | throws EAGAIN → heartbeat aborts | retries 3× → returns false on exhaustion |
| Tests | 0 EAGAIN-specific tests | 11 focused tests |

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- Scope: `heartbeat` / `session-store` / `workspace`
- Security: No security impact (local filesystem retry only)

### 5. Live model proof (Linux gateway)

```
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --model zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B \
    --session-key agent:default:issue-99994-proof \
    --message "Say exactly: EAGAIN (errno -11) on Linux means..." \
    --timeout 180

[assistant] EAGAIN (errno -11) on Linux means a filesystem read cannot
complete immediately because the kernel is racing with a concurrent
write-rename of the same file. A retry after a short delay usually succeeds.
[agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
```

### 6. Autoreview

```
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.95)
```

target.title: feat: add durable routines registry
target.body:
Closes #98515

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has cron jobs, tasks, heartbeat, commitments, and channel/session delivery primitives, but no first-class durable registry for recurring team-operations routines. Operators can schedule work today, but they cannot create, inspect, pause, delete, or recover a typed routine as one durable product object with ownership, delivery target, run status, and replay-safe mutation semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the smallest complete routine slice: a typed routine registry backed by the shared SQLite state DB, Gateway RPC methods, CLI entrypoints, an agent-tool entrypoint, and a schedule trigger that delegates execution to the canonical cron service rather than creating a second scheduler. The design keeps cron as the scheduler owner and routines as the durable registry owner, with internal create/toggle stages so retries recover safely after partial persistence or scheduler failures.

Non-goals for this draft: no Control UI yet, no channel-watch/repository-event/webhook triggers yet, no duplicate scheduler, and no transcript attachment. The trigger model is shaped so those future triggers can share the same routine subsystem instead of growing a second path.

AI-assisted implementation and review were used for this draft PR.

## User Impact

Users and operators can now use `openclaw routines`, Gateway RPC, or the Gateway agent tool to create, list, inspect, enable, disable, and delete durable scheduled routines. Routine inspection shows owner, delivery target, enabled/deleted state, last and next run visibility, status, and last error context. Repeated create/toggle/delete calls are idempotent, and restart/replay behavior preserves the intended routine state instead of silently losing a schedule toggle or rolling scheduler state backward.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `786ba1e63a6953c9c12c95fa99abe3b5aaffe7d3`, rebased on `origin/main` `5bcd25f0fb6de3cc2ba6b6a7688a9361eb355143`.
- LOC gate after final rebase: total 51 files `+6542/-409`; production 27 files `+3103/-390`, tests 11 files `+2805/-0`, docs 9 files `+359/-19`, generated protocol/state files 4 files `+275/-0`. Remaining positive production LOC is concentrated in the routine service durability/recovery state machine, narrow CLI/Gateway/protocol entrypoints, and shared cron validation/scope helpers that delete duplicated cron Gateway policy rather than creating a second scheduler.
- Exact-head local sanity passed: `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`, `pnpm docs:list`, `pnpm protocol:check`, and clean `git status --porcelain=v1`.
- Focused local runtime proof passed before the final app/extension-only rebases: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <routines/cron/Gateway/CLI/protocol/session/tool-result-truncation tests>` completed 5 shards / 156 tests, and targeted `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched runtime/test files>` passed. The later rebases touched only iOS/Android/Discord/Feishu owner files outside the routines/cron/Gateway/protocol lane.
- Testbox-through-Crabbox exact routine scenario passed with provider `blacksmith-testbox`, id `tbx_01kwh57ehx56t754rqjxqttskg`, Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28582551404. The proof matched exact tree `0b6d7d0814271c196c8fae82170f3590c1f12bde`, built the branch, started an isolated local Gateway, approved the staged device scope request, and drove `openclaw routines list/create/list/get/disable/enable/delete` through the public CLI and Gateway RPC. Final assertion output: `{"routineId":"proof-daily","cronJobId":"routine-cron-61f944366f18f9191d29a9b0425f6694","backing":"linked","status":"enabled","deleted":true,"persistentTarget":"session:agent:ops:main","isolatedTarget":"isolated","isolatedDelivery":"none"}`.

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint before building inbound context. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without adding repeated thread-history requests to normal same-session follow-ups.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts`: 72 passed; covers stable `route.sessionKey`, stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, and reset-session refetch.

target.title: improve(ui): flatten chat tool-call rows into a scannable list
target.body:
Closes #99760

## What Problem This Solves

Tool calls in the Control UI chat render as heavily decorated nested cards: the `Activity: N tools` group draws a bordered card, every tool message inside it draws another bubble box, and the summary button on top adds an accent gradient, an inset highlight, and a `0 8px 22px` drop shadow. Long tool summaries wrap across several lines. Dense agent sessions become hard to scan — a single 8-tool activity group fills an entire viewport.

Part of the box stacking is a CSS ordering bug: `components.css` begins with `@import "./chat.css"`, so its legacy `.chat-bubble` and `.chat-tool-card` blocks load after `chat/grouped.css`/`chat/tool-cards.css` and override the intended `.chat-bubble--tool-shell` resets (`padding: 0; border: 0; background: transparent`). Each tool row therefore leaks a full bubble box underneath the summary pill.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool rows are now flat one-line rows (chevron + tool icon + label + mono detail, ellipsized), the activity group header is a flat clickable row, and its body is grouped by a thin left rule instead of a card. Expanded tool detail keeps soft tinted input/output blocks without card chrome; canvas/document previews keep their frame because they embed external content. Error states remain explicit (red icon/label plus `Error` badge, error groups still auto-expand). The duplicated legacy chat-bubble/tool-card CSS in `components.css` is deleted and the canonical `.chat-bubble` base in `chat/grouped.css` is reconciled to today's computed style, so normal user/assistant bubbles render unchanged. Dead render paths (`renderToolCardSidebar`, never-taken `renderToolDataBlock` branches) and their orphaned CSS are removed.

## User Impact

Chat sessions with tool activity are dramatically denser and calmer: an 8-tool activity group shrinks from roughly a full screen of stacked cards to a few compact rows, in both light and dark themes. Collapsed rows clamp to one line; the full command and output remain one click away. No behavior changes: expand/collapse, error badges, sidebar open, and previews all work as before.

## Evidence

Before/after with the same seeded conversation (mock gateway fixture, light and dark, collapsed/expanded/detail states):
